title: Where the Moon Came From
objective: After this level you can describe the giant-impact explanation for the Moon’s origin and the evidence for it.
summary: The Moon most likely formed from debris after a Mars-sized body hit the young Earth about 4.5 billion years ago.

cards.headline: The Moon may be made of pieces of Earth.
cards.body: The leading explanation starts with a crash between the young Earth and a whole Mars-sized world. The Moon is what the crash left behind.

cards.headline: The giant impact
cards.body: About 4.5 billion years ago, a Mars-sized body that scientists call Theia is thought to have slammed into the young Earth. The collision flung debris out around Earth, and that debris gathered to form the Moon. Remember the Sun's age from Level 2, about 4.6 billion years? The Moon showed up early in the story, not long after Earth itself. Earth's worst day, and it got a Moon out of it.

cards.headline: The clues
cards.body: How do you check a crash nobody saw? Start with the Moon rocks Apollo astronauts brought back: they're chemically very similar to rocks from Earth's mantle. The Moon also has only a small iron core compared with Earth. And when scientists run computer simulations of a giant impact, out comes a Moon with an Earth-like makeup and a small iron core. Not proof, but every clue points the same way: back to Earth.

cards.headline: Moon origin: reconstructed
learned: The Moon likely formed from a giant impact
A Mars-sized body (Theia) hit the young Earth
That was about 4.5 billion years ago
Moon rocks closely match Earth’s mantle

questions.prompt: Put the giant impact story in order, from first to last.
questions.explanation: Theia slammed into the young Earth, the collision flung debris out around Earth, and that debris gathered to form the Moon.

questions.prompt: Which clue supports the idea that the Moon formed from material blasted off Earth?

options.label: The Moon is covered in thousands of impact craters
The Moon always keeps the same face toward Earth
options.rationale: That’s about its spin, not its origin.

options.label: The Moon’s dark “seas” are made of ancient lava
Moon rocks are chemically very similar to Earth’s mantle

questions.explanation: Apollo samples closely match Earth’s mantle rocks, and the Moon has only a small iron core: what you’d expect from debris of Earth’s outer layers.

questions.prompt: From Level 2: the Sun is about 4.6 billion years old. The Moon’s age of about 4.5 billion years suggests it _____.

options.label: formed a few million years ago
options.rationale: Billions of years is anything but recent.

options.label: came from another star system
options.rationale: Its age fits our own solar system’s early history.

questions.explanation: The Moon is only a little younger than the Sun, so it formed early, not long after Earth itself.
